arxiv-2204-14199.title: Preoperative brain tumor imaging: models and software for segmentation and standardized reporting
arxiv-2204-14199.creator: David Bouget
arxiv-2204-14199.description: Abstract For patients suffering from brain tumor, prognosis estimation and treatment decisions are made by a multidisciplinary team based on a set of preoperative MR scans. Currently, the lack of standardized and automatic methods for tumor detection and generation of clinical reports, incorporating a wide range of tumor characteristics, represents a major hurdle.

arxiv-2205-07983.title: Test-Time Adaptation with Shape Moments for Image Segmentation
arxiv-2205-07983.creator: Mathilde Bateson, Hervé Lombaert, Ismail Ben Ayed
arxiv-2205-07983.description: Abstract Supervised learning is well-known to fail at generalization under distribution shifts. In typical clinical settings, the source data is inaccessible and the target distribution is represented with a handful of samples: adaptation can only happen at test time on a few (or even a single) subject(s).

arxiv-2211-14676.title: Maximizing the Probability of Fixation in the Positional Voter Model
arxiv-2211-14676.creator: Petros Petsinis, Andreas Pavlogiannis, Panagiotis Karras
arxiv-2211-14676.description: Abstract The Voter model is a well-studied stochastic process that models the invasion of a novel trait A A (e.g., a new opinion, social meme, genetic mutation, magnetic spin) in a network of individuals (agents, people, genes, particles) carrying an existing resident trait B B .

arxiv-2212-00601.title: Multi-rater Prism: Learning self-calibrated medical image segmentation from multiple raters Journal: Journal of Medical Image Analysis
arxiv-2212-00601.creator: Junde Wu, Huihui Fang, Yehui Yang, Yuanpei Liu, Jing Gao, Lixin Duan, Weihua Yang, Yanwu Xu
arxiv-2212-00601.description: Abstract In medical image segmentation, it is often necessary to collect opinions from multiple experts to make the final decision. This clinical routine helps to mitigate individual bias. But when data is multiply annotated, standard deep learning models are often not applicable.

arxiv-2311-05459.title: Observational constraints on the origin of the elements. VIII. Constraining the Barium, Strontium and Yttrium chemical evolution in metal-poor stars
arxiv-2311-05459.creator: G. Guiglion, M. Bergemann, N. Storm, J. Lian, G. Cescutti, A. Serenelli
arxiv-2311-05459.description: Abstract Context. The chemical evolution history of slow neutron-capture elements in the Milky Way is still a matter of debate, especially in the metal-poor regime ([Fe/H]¡-1). Aims. Recently Lian et al. 2023 , thanks to Gaia -ESO spectroscopic data, studied the chemical evolution of neutron-capture elements in the regime [Fe/H]¿-1.

arxiv-2312-16661.title: The AMIGA sample of isolated galaxies – Effects of Environment on Angular momentum The AMIGA sample of isolated galaxies – Effects of Environment on Angular momentum – 19
arxiv-2312-16661.creator: A. Sorgho, L. Verdes-Montenegro, K. M. Hess, M. G. Jones, T. H. Jarrett, S. Sanchez-Expósito, J. Garrido
arxiv-2312-16661.description: Abstract We investigate the relationship between the baryonic angular momentum and mass for a sample of 36 isolated disc galaxies with resolved H i kinematics and infrared WISE photometry drawn from – and representative in terms of morphologies, stellar masses and H i -to-star fraction of – the carefully-constructed AMIGA sample of isolated galaxies.

arxiv-2401-07237.title: Distilling Event Sequence Knowledge From Large Language Models
arxiv-2401-07237.creator: Somin Wadhwa, Oktie Hassanzadeh, Debarun Bhattacharjya, Ken Barker, Jian Ni
arxiv-2401-07237.description: Abstract Event sequence models have been found to be highly effective in the analysis and prediction of events. Building such models requires availability of abundant high-quality event sequence data. In certain applications, however, clean structured event sequences are not available, and automated sequence extraction results in data that is too noisy and incomplete.

arxiv-2403-08476.title: Emergent Continuous Time Crystal in Dissipative Quantum Spin System without Driving
arxiv-2403-08476.creator: Shu Yang, Zeqing Wang, Libin Fu, Jianwen Jie
arxiv-2403-08476.description: Abstract Time crystals are a nonequilibrium phase of matter that extend fundamental spontaneous symmetry breaking into the temporal dimension, typically requiring external driving for their realization. Here, we explore the nonequilibrium phase diagram of a two-dimensional dissipative Heisenberg spin system without external coherent or incoherent driving.

arxiv-2403-15661.title: An Embedding of Schwartz Distributions in the Algebra of Asymptotic Functions
arxiv-2403-15661.creator: Michael Oberguggenberger
arxiv-2403-15661.description: Abstract We present a solution of the problem of multiplication of Schwartz distributions by embedding the space of distributions into a differential algebra of generalized functions, called in the paper “asymptotic function”, similar to but different from J. F. Colombeau’s algebras of new generalized functions.

arxiv-2408-01612.title: Data-Driven Machine Learning Approaches for Predicting In-Hospital Sepsis Mortality
arxiv-2408-01612.creator: Arseniy Shumilov 1, Yueting Zhu 1, Negin Ashrafi 1, Armin Abdollahi 1, Greg Placencia 2, Kamiar Alaei 3, Maryam Pishgar 1
arxiv-2408-01612.description: Abstract Sepsis is a severe condition responsible for many deaths in the United States and worldwide, making accurate prediction of outcomes crucial for timely and effective treatment. Previous studies employing machine learning faced limitations in feature selection and model interpretability, reducing their clinical applicability.

arxiv-2506-11746.title: complex harmonic maps and rank 2 higher teichmüller theory
arxiv-2506-11746.creator: Christian El Emam, Nathaniel Sagman
arxiv-2506-11746.description: Abstract . We initiate and develop the theory of complex harmonic maps to holomorphic Riemannian symmetric spaces, which we make use of to study complex analytic aspects of higher Teichmüller theory, with a focus on rank 2 2 Hitchin components.

arxiv-2507-16562.title: Evaluating Social Acceptance of eXtended Reality (XR) Agent Technology: A User Study (Extended Version)
arxiv-2507-16562.creator: Megha Quamara, Viktor Schmuck, Cristina Iani, Axel Primavesi, Alexander Plaum, Luca Viganò
arxiv-2507-16562.description: Abstract In this paper, we present the findings of a user study that evaluated the social acceptance of eXtended Reality (XR) agent technology, focusing on a remotely accessible, web-based XR training system developed for journalists. This system involves user interaction with a virtual avatar, enabled by a modular toolkit.

arxiv-2604-18872.creator: Alex McAvoy

arxiv-2606-11402.title: GraphGP: Scalable Gaussian Processes with Vecchia’s Approximation
arxiv-2606-11402.creator: Benjamin Dodge, Philipp Frank, Susan E. Clark

doe-osti-2999881-biologically-influenced.creator: Swanson, Juliet S.
doe-osti-2999881-biologically-influenced.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. This report provides an update to a previously issued report on the bioassociation of the +3 actinide analog, neodymium, with Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (WIPP) microbial isolates (LCO ACP-32, <em>Biologically Influenced Transport of the +3 Actinide Oxidation State from the WIPP

pmc-10655246.title: Decoding the Interplay between Topology and Surface Charge in Graphene Oxide Membranes During Humidity Induced Swelling
pmc-10655246.creator: Mohd Rafie
pmc-10655246.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Graphene oxide (GO) membranes are known to have a complex morphology that depends on the degree of oxidation of the graphene flake and the membrane preparation technique. In this study, using Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate the mechanism of swelling of GO membranes exposed to different relative humidity (RH) values and show how this is intimately related to the graphene surface chemistry.

pmc-11376342.title: Active template synthesis
pmc-11376342.creator: Romain Jamagne, Martin J. Power, Zhi-Hui Zhang, Germán Zango, Benjamin Gibber, David A. Leigh
pmc-11376342.description: The active template synthesis of mechanically interlocked molecular architectures exploits the dual ability of various structural elements (metals or, in the case of metal-free active template synthesis, particular arrangements of functional groups) to serve as both a template for the organisation of building blocks and as a catalyst to facilitate the formation of covalent bonds between them.

pmc-11509135.title: Performance Evaluation of Pebble Concrete for Pavement: A Study on the Sucre Highway Project
pmc-11509135.creator: Zhuqing Feng, Jue Lu, Simin Liu, Jingliang Xia, Jing Wang, Faguang Leng, Xinxin Ma
pmc-11509135.description: Bolivia has abundant pebbles, while the supply of crushed stone is limited and unstable. Thus, the resource utilization of local pebble as a coarse aggregate and the guarantee of concrete durability are the key scientific issues in the Sucre Highway Project. In this paper, a comparative analysis was conducted of the performance of crushed stone concrete and pebble concrete.

pmc-11641765.title: Replacing 2 Gy Per Fraction Equivalent Dose with Fractionation-Specific Biological Equivalent Dose for Normal Tissues
pmc-11641765.creator: Wei Luo, William St Clair
pmc-11641765.description: The 2 Gy per fraction equivalent dose (EQD2) is an important quantity used in determining equivalent prescription doses for different fractionation regimens and evaluating different fractionation regimens, but it does not match its definition when it is used for normal tissues. We propose to use the fractionation-specific biological equivalent dose to determine normal tissue dose constraints for different fractionation regimens.

pmc-11654136.title: Progressive decrease in partial pressure of end-tidal CO2 during posterior spinal fusion surgery in a child with idiopathic scoliosis and pectus excavatum: a case report
pmc-11654136.creator: Yan Xu, Yanjun Lin, Chunling Jiang, Li Zhou
pmc-11654136.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundScoliosis surgery performed in a prone position may result in thoracic anatomical compression and alter local hemodynamics, increasing surgical risk, especially in patients with pectus excavatum. Most commonly, refractory hypotension is the first symptom of these circulatory changes. Here, we report a case with scoliosis and pectus excavatum under posterior spinal fusion that presented as a progressive decrease in the partial pressure of end-tidal CO2 (PETCO2) as the first symptom in the prone position.

pmc-11691953.title: ROLES OF LONELINESS, STRESS, AND RELIGIOSITY IN SUICIDE IDEATION IN A SAMPLE OF SUB-SAHARAN AFRICAN OLDER ADULTS
pmc-11691953.creator: Genevieve Ebulum, John Eze, Obinna Ezeihuoma, Crystal Njoku, JohnBosco Chukwuorji
pmc-11691953.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Suicidal behaviour in older adults is a fundamental public health problem globally and the highest suicide rates occur in the low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). However, there is limited research on suicidality among older adults especially in sub-Saharan Africa. We sought to find out whether loneliness, stress and religiosity would significantly predict suicide ideation among Nigerian older adults (N = 500).

pmc-12389088.title: Berries from Luzuriaga radicans Ruiz & Pav.: A Southern Chile Climbing Shrub as a Source of Antioxidants Against Chronic Diseases
pmc-12389088.creator: Sebastian Scharf, Javier Romero-Parra, Peter Winterhalter, Alfredo Torres-Benítez, Recep Gök, Mario J Simirgiotis, Marcello Salvatore Lenucci
pmc-12389088.description: In recent years, numerous studies have emerged on the biological activities of endemic berries from the Valdivian Forest and their potential for therapeutic use. However, some species appear to have been relatively neglected. The objective of this study was to conduct, for the first time, a phytochemical composition analysis of a hydroalcoholic extract of Luzuriaga radicans Ruiz & Pav.

pmc-12606819.title: Analysis of suspected serious adverse drug reactions reported with traditional medicines from the United Nations Asia region in WHO vigibase
pmc-12606819.creator: Chandan N, Manish Barvaliya, Tejas Patel, Chetan AC, Harsha Hegde, Banappa Unger
pmc-12606819.description: BackgroundTraditional medicines (TMs) are not regulated like conventional drugs in many countries, and they are often perceived as safe, which leads to large-scale self-medication. There is limited safety information available for TMs. Thus, including them in pharmacovigilance systems is crucial for systematically gathering and evaluating adverse drug reactions (ADRs) to enhance safety and prevent harm with their use.

pmc-12696788.title: Tracking and Controlling Monolayer Water in Gold Nanogaps using Extreme Plasmonic Spectroscopy
pmc-12696788.creator: Elle W. Wyatt, Sarah May Sibug‐Torres, Rakesh Arul, Marika Niihori, Tabitha Jones, James W. Beattie, Bart de Nijs, Jeremy J. Baumberg
pmc-12696788.description: Nanogaps are ubiquitous across science and technology, confining molecules and thus changing chemistries that influence many areas such as catalysis, corrosion, photochemistry, and sensing. However, in ambient conditions, it is unclear how water solvates nanogaps and even if nominally dry, what water structure persists.

pmc-12736918.title: Forecasting Energy Demand in Quicklime Manufacturing: A Data-Driven Approach
pmc-12736918.creator: Jersson X. Leon-Medina, John Erick Fonseca Gonzalez, Nataly Yohana Callejas Rodriguez, Mario Eduardo González Niño, Saúl Andrés Hernández Moreno, Wilman Alonso Pineda-Munoz, Claudia Patricia Siachoque Celys, Bernardo Umbarila Suarez, Francesc Pozo
pmc-12736918.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study presents a deep learning-based framework for forecasting energy demand in a quicklime production company, aiming to enhance operational efficiency and enable data-driven decision-making for industrial scalability. Using one year of real electricity consumption data, the methodology integrates temporal and operational variables—such as load profile, active power, shift indicators, and production-related proxies—to capture the dynamics of energy usage throughout the manufacturing process.

pmc-12755311.title: ZnO-modified carbon paste electrode for electrochemical sensing of dopamine in the presence of tyrosine
pmc-12755311.creator: Ali Obaid Imarah, Nada Hasan, Mustafa G Alabbasi
pmc-12755311.description: Background and purposeDopamine, 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine, functions as a catecholamine neurotransmitter in the brain, sending messages to other neurons to regulate information transmission to other areas of the brain, govern movement, and alter brain activity. Tyrosine undergoes an enzymatic process in the pharmaceutical industry to produce dopamine. Thus, it is crucial to measure both tyrosine and dopamine in bodily fluids simultaneously.

pmc-13380617.title: Practitioner perceptions of biodiversity criteria for solar suitability analyses in the United States
pmc-13380617.creator: Daphne Condon, Michael O. Levin, Adam B. Smith, Toni Lyn Morelli, Noah Z. Krasner, Emma Forester, Chevon Holmes, Benjamin P. Narwold, Elizabeth L. Kalies, Grace C. Wu, Meaghan R. Gade, Roland Kays, Freya Robinson, Rebecca R. Hernandez
pmc-13380617.description: Acceleration of large-scale solar energy deployment can pose competition for land with biodiversity conservation areas. Solar suitability analyses (SSAs) help identify low-conflict zones for solar development, yet limited work defines which biodiversity-relevant criteria (BRCs) are essential for SSAs or whether supporting data are available.

pmc-13403899.title: Comparison of the hemodynamic effects of ropivacaine versus bupivacaine for elective cesarean delivery under combined spinal–epidural anesthesia: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13403899.creator: Fanshu Ni, Haiyin Ji, Ping Zhao
pmc-13403899.description: BackgroundWomen with term pregnancies undergoing cesarean delivery under combined spinal and epidural anesthesia (CSEA) usually present with hemodynamic variability and a high incidence of hypotension. Among the commonly used anesthetic drugs for CSEA, ropivacaine reduces the incidence of hypotension compared with bupivacaine.

pmc-13522822.title: Examining current E-cigarette use among U.S. adults by groups stratified by demographic characteristics, 2014–2023
pmc-13522822.creator: Elizabeth L Seaman Jones, Jamie Cordova, Margaret Mahoney, Kristy Marynak, Jeremy Morton
pmc-13522822.description: ObjectiveThis study explores current e-cigarette use from 2014 to 2023 among U.S. adults stratified by demographic groups.MethodsRepeated, cross-sectional self-respondent data from the Tobacco Use Supplement to the Current Population Survey (TUS-CPS) from 2014 to 2015, 2018–2019 and 2022–2023 were analyzed. Self-response and replicate weights were applied for nationally representative estimates.

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The purposes of the Rural Business Investment Program established under this subchapter are— (1) to promote economic development and the creation of wealth and job opportunities in rural areas and among individuals living in those areas by encouraging developmental capital investments.
